PolyStrata 

 English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · Deutsch · Français · Español · Português · Türkçe

 Run large AI models on your own PC 
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, LFM2.5, Flint, Qwen3.6, Clover, Ornith 1.5, Gemma 4, Tiel Coder, MiniCPM-V and Kolibri 1 · free and open source 

 

 

 
 Claude Code on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q3 K M, on the laptop with the 8 GB card, in real time: it adds a --json option to a small program, writes a test for it and runs the tests. The server had read Claude Code's system prompt when it started ( "warm start": true ). 

 
 A voxel pagoda garden, 1 shot prompt running on an RTX 5070 with Strata (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3 S, 128K context) ·
 full video (49 s) 

PolyStrata runs large AI models on a normal PC, models that usually need a server. They chat, write code and work
with your apps and coding agents. Nothing leaves your PC.

It runs twelve models, on two engines:

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on an NVIDIA or AMD graphics card with
 12 GB or more, on Windows or Linux. It also reads pictures. Its engine is the Strata project's, unchanged.

The other eleven run on an engine written for PolyStrata, with one NVIDIA card or two: on Linux, and all but GLM 5.3 Flash and
DeepSeek V4 Flash on Windows too. They are experimental: they have run on one PC with a 32 GB card, and the eight smaller ones on a laptop
with an 8 GB card as well.

- GLM 5.3 Flash , the largest: a file of 79 to 114 GB, most of which stays in RAM.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash , a file of 91 GB, most of which stays in RAM too. Its memory of a
 conversation is small: a 128K context takes 0.7 GB more VRAM than 32K.
- LFM2.5-24B-A2B by Liquid AI, a file of 11 to 25 GB. Most of its layers have no attention, so a
 long conversation takes little VRAM: a 128K context takes 2 GB more than 32K. Its license allows commercial use
 only to companies with less than 10 million dollars of yearly revenue.
- Flint 40B-A2.5B by Recursive, made for coding agents: a file of 18 to 42 GB. Most of its layers
 look back only 513 tokens, so a long conversation takes little VRAM: a 128K context takes 2.6 GB more than 32K.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B , a file of 13 to 23 GB. It also reads pictures.
- Clover-35B-A3B-Preview by DiffuSpace, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B trained further to also write a
 block of tokens at once: a file of 13 to 21 GB. It reads text only.
- Ornith 1.5 , which has Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's architecture and other weights: a file of 14 to 24 GB. It
 also reads pictures.
- Gemma 4 26B-A4B , a file of 11 to 17 GB. It also reads pictures.
- Tiel Coder 35B-A3B , Ornith 1.5 quantized for coding agents by peculiar-ragdoll: a file of
 14 to 23 GB. It also reads pictures.
- MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B by OpenBMB, which has Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's architecture and weights of its
 own, made to read pictures: a file of 16 to 29 GB.
- Kolibri 1 by Aleph Alpha, which writes German as well as English: a file of 29 to 48 GB,
 most of which stays in RAM beside a small card.

The server can change between installed models while it runs (how).

PolyStrata was created by VecSzn.
PolyStrata is built on Strata by Niko1221.
Why it is a separate repo, AMD and smaller cards, fine-tunes and other questions: FAQ.

 How fast is it?

A token is about ¾ of a word.

- Writes answers: how fast the reply appears in a short chat. 60 tokens per second is faster than you can read.
- Reads your prompt: how fast it takes in what you send (a document, code or a chat history).

The table gives the size the installer takes for each model, in tokens per second. Every size's numbers, the comparison with llama.cpp and how they were measured are on each model's page.

 Model Laptop with an 8 GB card writes / reads RTX 5090 writes / reads Every size 
 --- ---: ---: --- 
 LFM2.5-24B-A2B 70-73 / 3,590-3,620 480-485 / 23,390-23,460 LFM2.5 
 Flint 40B-A2.5B 61-63 / 2,000-2,010 251-252 / 12,900 Flint 
 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 94-100 / 1,690 394-395 / 7,800-7,810 Qwen3.6 
 Clover-35B-A3B-Preview 68-73 / 1,560-1,700 not measured Clover 
 Ornith 1.5 76-82 / 1,620 316-319 / 8,040-8,110 Ornith 
 Gemma 4 26B-A4B 92-93 / 2,240 353-356 / 8,420-8,480 Gemma 4 
 Tiel Coder 35B-A3B 83 / 1,700 337-345 / 8,080-8,110 Tiel Coder 
 MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B 64 / 1,150 308-311 / 7,910-7,950 MiniCPM-V 
 Kolibri 1 not measured 189-192 / 4,980-5,070 Kolibri 1 
 GLM 5.3 Flash does not run: needs a 32 GB card 59-66 / 820 GLM 
 DeepSeek V4 Flash does not run: needs a 32 GB card 56 / 1,040 DeepSeek 

Laptop: RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB), Core i7-14700HX, 32 GB RAM. Workstation: RTX 5090 (32 GB), Xeon Platinum 8470Q (25 vCPU), 90 to 120 GB RAM. Flint is UD-Q3 K XL on the laptop, the size the installer takes with 32 GB of RAM, and UD-Q4 K XL on the workstation. Kolibri 1 is Q2 K on the workstation; the installer takes Q4 K M there, which was not measured.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on the Strata project's engine and was measured by that project on a PC with an RTX 5070 (12 GB) and 64 GB of RAM: IQ2 XS writes at 79 and reads a 32K prompt at 2,090 (every size).

The eleven models of PolyStrata's own engine were measured with its benchmark, which you can run on your PC:
 python polystrata.py benchmark --model --prompt-tokens 24000 
(what it sends and prints).
What others measured on their own cards, and how to compare with llama.cpp on yours:
community results.
On the laptop PolyStrata read prompts 2.7 to 3.5 times as fast as llama.cpp b11540 and wrote 1.5 to 1.8 times
as fast, with Qwen3.6 and with Tiel Coder (the two runs).

 How much RAM it keeps

Since 0.1.45-poly.7 the engine of the eleven models keeps less of your RAM: it no longer holds the parts of the
model file that are already on the graphics card. On the laptop, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B after a 32,000-token prompt held
17.9 GiB with 0.1.45-poly.6 and holds 13.1 GiB now, and writes as fast. Under Linux it went from 17.8 to 12.6 GiB.

To hold less, add "--ram-experts-mib", "6144" to the "args" list of strata- .json 
(where) and restart. The engine then holds that many MiB of RAM for the
experts t

install.title: Install
install.html:
Let your AI set it up

Do you use an AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, ...)? Paste this into it:

Set up PolyStrata on this PC for me: https://github.com/simplexai-labs/PolyStrata - follow docs/AI_SETUP.md in that repository.

It checks your graphics card, RAM and disk and picks the model that fits. Then it installs and starts it and tells you how to connect your apps. AI tools can also install, start and stop PolyStrata through its MCP server.

Or do it yourself

Download PolyStrata and unzip it (or git clone it). Windows: double-click START-HERE.bat. Linux: run ./setup.sh in the PolyStrata folder.

Mac (Apple Silicon, M1 to M5, macOS 15 or newer): install Apple's Command Line Tools once (xcode-select --install in Terminal; Xcode itself is not needed). Then open Terminal in the PolyStrata folder and run ./setup.sh. It builds the Mac engine on your Mac (about 7 minutes), asks the same questions, downloads the model and starts it. Next time, ./setup.sh starts it right away. Which size fits your Mac and how fast it is: docs/MAC.md. By default it sets up Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. ./setup.sh --family qwen36 or --family lfm25 sets up Qwen3.6 or LFM2.5 instead, on strata-poly's Metal engine, as a beta: on an M5 Ultra, Qwen3.6 UD-Q2_K_XL wrote 134 tokens/s in a short chat and read a 3,768-token prompt at 2,978 tokens/s. Setup also offers GLM, DeepSeek, Ornith, Gemma 4, Tiel Coder and MiniCPM-V on a Mac, but they have not been run there with their real weights. Kolibri, Flint and Clover need an NVIDIA or AMD card.

The installer finds your card and sets up the right engine for it. It asks you a few questions:

  • which model and which size,
  • how much context (how much text the model keeps in mind),
  • whether it should read pictures (GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, LFM2.5, Flint, Clover and Kolibri 1 read none).

Press Enter each time for the recommended answer. Then it downloads the model (about 70 GB for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 79 to 114 GB for GLM 5.3 Flash, 91 GB for DeepSeek V4 Flash, 29 to 48 GB for Kolibri 1, 11 to 42 GB for the other eight) and starts it. If the download stops, run it again: it continues where it left off. Your browser opens the PolyStrata app at http://127.0.0.1:8080.

All twelve are in the installer's list of models. ./setup.sh --family glm, deepseek, lfm25, flint, qwen36, clover, ornith, gemma4, tiel, minicpmv or kolibri goes straight to one (what it asks and writes).

While the model starts, your PC can be slow or stop responding for 1-3 minutes (longest the first time). PolyStrata loads 35-55 GB into your RAM and locks part of it for the graphics card. This is normal. Wait, and don't close the window. The window shows what PolyStrata is doing.

Next time, run START-HERE.bat (or ./setup.sh) again. It starts right away and downloads nothing twice. Close its window to stop the model. UPDATE.bat (./update.sh) updates PolyStrata without starting it. Updating, Docker, several cards, where the files go and every option: docs/INSTALL.md.

Is it fast on your PC? Run BENCH.bat (./bench.sh): about 5-10 minutes, it measures chat, 4K/16K prompts and an agent-style session with your own settings and writes a report to share (how).

usage.title: Using it
usage.html:
All twelve models are used the same way: the same app, the same API.


The app's Monitor (left) while a coding agent writes the pagoda garden from the video (right). A screenshot from Strata.

  • In the browser: open http://127.0.0.1:8080. It has Chat, a live Monitor of the model and your GPU/CPU/RAM, and About with the settings and addresses.
  • As your personal agent: download Linger for Mac (Apple silicon) · Windows · Linux.
  • Your apps and coding agents: add an "OpenAI-compatible" provider with the base URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. Any API key and any model name work.
    • Apps that use Anthropic's API: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages (Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080, and "fit_max_tokens": true in strata-<model>.json (why)).
    • Codex CLI and other apps that use the OpenAI Responses API: /v1/responses (setup).
  • Thinking: choose off, low, medium or high in the chat menu or in your app's "reasoning effort". Off is the fastest. High is best for hard questions.
  • From your phone or another PC: START-HERE.bat --setup --host 0.0.0.0 --api-key <secret>. Always set a key.

Where they differ:

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GLM 5.3 Flash DeepSeek V4 Flash LFM2.5-24B-A2B Flint 40B-A2.5B Kolibri 1 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, Ornith 1.5, Gemma 4 26B-A4B, Tiel Coder 35B-A3B, MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B
Pictures Say yes to "Images?" in setup. Then click Picture in the chat, or attach pictures in your app. AMD cards read pictures on Linux through the processor; on Windows they can't yet. Not yet. It reads text only. It reads text only. It reads text only. It reads text only. Say yes to "Images?" in setup, then as with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. On a card with less than 16 GB the picture encoder runs on the processor, and a picture takes a few seconds. Clover reads text only.
Several requests One at a time by default, the others wait. "parallel": 2 answers several at once (BATCHING.md); on a 12 GB card each answer gets slower. One at a time, the others wait. One at a time, the others wait. One at a time, the others wait. One at a time, the others wait. One at a time, the others wait. One at a time, the others wait.
Several conversations The last one is kept, so follow-up messages start in seconds. Two engine arguments keep several in RAM (details). The last one is kept. Setup asks whether to keep several in RAM, so that an agent and its subagents take turns without their prompts being read again (how). As GLM 5.3 Flash. As GLM 5.3 Flash. As GLM 5.3 Flash. As GLM 5.3 Flash. As GLM 5.3 Flash.
Long prompts The first message of a chat is read in full, about 1 minute per 30,000 tokens. The first message is read in full, about 40 seconds per 30,000 tokens. The first message is read in full, about 29 seconds per 30,000 tokens. The first message is read in full: 30,000 tokens take 1.3 to 1.5 seconds on the workstation and 8 to 10 seconds on the 8 GB laptop. The first message is read in full: 30,000 tokens take about 2.3 seconds on the workstation and 15 to 22 seconds on the 8 GB laptop. The first message is read in full: 30,000 tokens take about 6 seconds on the workstation with Q2_K. The first message is read in full: 30,000 tokens take 4 to 5 seconds on the workstation and 14 to 27 seconds on the 8 GB laptop.

More: where your chats are stored, the API.

Optional: more speed on one card when the whole model fits in RAM

Two opt-in settings (by RubenTorney, #1904 and #1905). They help when you run one graphics card and your RAM holds every expert (PolyStrata's arena mode, for example Q2_0 or IQ3_XXS on a 64 GB PC). Open your config, strata-<model>.json in the PolyStrata data folder (where), and add:

  • Faster decode: "--adapt-async", "1" to the "args" list. The expert cache then updates on a helper thread instead of pausing the answer. Measured on an RTX 5070 (Windows, Q2_0): +4-5% decode, +7-10% on code and long documents. Answers can differ slightly from the default (they stay the same from run to run).
  • Faster prompt reading on Windows: "STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED": "1" in the "env" block. Windows can lock only about half the RAM for the graphics card; this locks the experts the card actually needs first. Measured on the RTX 5070: +4.4% prompt reading.
"args": [ ..., "--adapt-async", "1" ],
"env": { "STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED": "1" }

Restart PolyStrata (START-HERE.bat or ./setup.sh) after the change. To undo, remove the two entries.
